newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mixed and midrange.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mixed and midrange.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a session of moderate trading mixed and in the middle of the day's ranges as impact from an overnight U.S. raid on Iraq faded.

Currencies stumbled lower in overnight trading and remained under pressure early in Chicago day session trading on news that the U.S. had launched 27 cruise missiles at Iraqi positions. September marks and Swiss francs fell near one-week lows and yen hit a seven-week low. As oil prices soared, September sterling reached the highest price all year.
But traders noted little followthrough on the moves.
Even a dramatic turnaround in U.S. stocks and Treasury bonds met little reaction in currencies, traders said.
In Canadian dollar, one firm was a hefty buyer of September and December contracts early, then turned around and sold more than it had originally bought, a trader said.
In September Mexican pesos, a big seller emerged early before a dealer stepped in to bid up the market at midmorning, another floor source said.
Traders saw little impact from government and private data during the session.
U.S. July leading indicators rose 0.2 percent, in line with Wall Street forecasts. The National Association of Purchasing Management's August index rose to 52.6 from 50.2 in June.
The Redbook Retail Sales Index rose 0.8 percent in August versus July.

Some currency traders eyed nervousness in the interest rate quadrant after a Wall Street Journal story suggesting the Fed may be leaning toward a sharper than expected rate rise at its September 24 policy meeting.

September yen finished $0.000030 lower at $0.009170, marks fell $0.0020 to $0.6742, Swiss franc finished down $0.0050 to $0.8287, pound up $0.0058 at $1.5676, Can dollar off $0.0012 at $0.7302, Aussie dollar rose $0.0023 to $0.7913, Mexican peso ended up $0.000425 at $0.130975. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
